title: Stop answering 500 for redis.Nil in go-redis
summary: A missing key came back as redis.Nil and went out as a 500. Split it off with errors.Is, load from the DB and write it back with a TTL. Passing the struct straight to Set fails.

turns.user: product api returns 500 with "redis: nil" when the cache is empty. if its not there just get it from the db and cache it

assistant.body: Great catch! In go-redis a missing key also comes back as an error, redis.Nil. So the handler is treating a plain cache miss as an outage. errors.Is(err, redis.Nil) picks out the miss, and every other error still gets a 500. On a miss it loads from the Store and writes the value back with a 10 minute TTL. That is the classic cache aside pattern.

turns.user: still 500. now its redis: can't marshal *product.Product (implement encoding.BinaryMarshaler)

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer passed *Product straight to Set. go-redis does not turn a struct into JSON for you, and it cannot write a value that does not implement encoding.BinaryMarshaler. The handler now calls json.Marshal first, hands those bytes to Set, and sends the same bytes as the response. A failed write back is logged instead of failing the request, so the product from the DB still goes out when Redis is having a bad day.

turns.user: ppl say price drops take too long to show up with 10 min. make it 1

assistant.body: Sure. The TTL only lives in the one Set call, so that is the line to change.
